A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same six-task study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model experiments on six tasks in Tables 1–6, plus tree-of-thought results and a vehicle-learning analysis in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds controlled task variations, steering experiments, failure examples and an original bootstrap analysis.

M1.justification: Appendices A.7 and C.6 introduce task-specific inference instructions directing reasoning toward bigrams or retrieval of matching license plates. These modify prompting procedures in supplementary conditions; the underlying models and original direct/CoT procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The six task families remain, but v4 adds simpler grammar distributions, faces with differing descriptions, binary face matching and vehicle classification with a binary oracle feature. Appendix G additionally analyzes 378 published model-task comparisons as a new data source, without rerunning those benchmarks.

E2.justification: The model comparator sets in Tables 1–6 are unchanged, and tree-of-thought was already evaluated in v1. v4 adds comparisons involving bigram-guided CoT and progressively stronger license-plate steering alongside ordinary prompting conditions (A.7, C.6).

E3.justification: New protocols include temperature sweeps over 4400 grammar problems, a balanced 100-problem binary face test and a vehicle-oracle experiment capped at seven iterations. The bootstrap analysis uses vehicle classification accuracy instead of rounds to permit aggregation. These supplement the retained main experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing tree-of-thought and learning-curve analyses, v4 tests grammar complexity, sampling temperature, face-task difficulty, image-ordering explanations, oracle features and steering strength. It also adds three failure examples and tests whether the task-selection heuristic disproportionately identifies CoT failures.

E5.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix G add two bootstrap tests, each using 100000 resamples of size 50, assessing failure magnitude and frequency. Appendix C.6 also reports independent trial counts and an uncertainty interval for steering experiments. Existing main-table p-values and learning-curve error bars are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the original tree-of-thought results retain their values. Substantial new results include direct/CoT accuracies of 61%/32% with differing face descriptions and 72%/62% for binary face matching; combined vehicle steering achieves perfect classification by iteration two in both conditions. These are newly evaluated conditions, not improvements to the original results.

T1.justification: The finite-state grammar definitions, logical-consistency formulation, Gaussian distractor construction and additive apartment-utility assumption are retained. v4 adds empirical procedures and interpretations, without new theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v1 presents two conditions as predicting CoT failures and describes the three mismatch tasks as showing no negative effects. v4 explicitly acknowledges mixed positive, neutral and negative effects and frames the approach as an imperfect heuristic. It also claims statistically demonstrated enrichment of failure cases and introduces a released six-task benchmark.

C2.justification: The logical-inconsistency explanation shifts from low baseline performance toward differences in formal-logic knowledge. New controls support interpretations concerning image ordering and distracting features, while successful steering qualifies CoT failures as dependent on its default reasoning strategy. Appendix F.1 adds explicit discussion of the apartment implementation favoring models and possible memory restrictions.

D1.justification: v4 supplies decoding temperatures and output-token budgets throughout Appendices A–F, including the o1 temperature exception and an 8000-token apartment budget. It also provides a repository link for the six task datasets. These substantially extend v1's construction instructions and prompts; newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to earlier runs.

R1.justification: v4 adds relevant work on fragile mathematical reasoning, CoT-related bias/toxicity and long-context retrieval, including Mirzadeh, Shaikh and Liu. It also positions the heuristic empirically against Sprague's metastudy. The principal psychology-based research positioning remains intact; publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, task discussions and concluding discussion are extensively rewritten. Task-specific Hypothesis paragraphs become Human failure descriptions, the numbered limitations/future-directions structure is consolidated, and a heuristic-effectiveness section is introduced. v4 also repairs malformed prose in v1.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one to two columns, with substantially resized tables and revised captions. The existing learning curve moves from appendix Figure 5 to main-text Figure 2. v4 adds two task-variation figures and three failure-example tables, while relocating many appendix tables to the document's end.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens the evidence through targeted robustness and steering tests and corrects the categorical no-harm claim that conflicted with v1's own tables. Dataset access and decoding details improve reproducibility. Appendix A.7 still mixes a stated subset experiment with full-dataset reference accuracies, limiting that comparison, but the broader gains in evidential support and calibration of claims are substantial.
